scenarios.name: Modern World
scenarios.description: The world of the mid-2020s with present-day borders (Natural Earth, UN boundary view). Every recognised state and Taiwan is playable; overseas dependencies belong to their sovereign states.
scenarios.approximations: Population and GDP per country are rounded c. 2025 estimates; their spread across provinces, terrain, and starting armies are model estimates. No wars are active at start.

scenarios.name: Height of Rome
scenarios.description: August 117: Trajan is dead, Hadrian takes the purple and the Roman Empire stands at its greatest extent, while Parthia recovers Mesopotamia, the Kushans rule the road to India and Eastern Han China faces the Xianbei on the steppe.
scenarios.approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces, so frontiers such as the Rhine-Danube limes, Hadrian's later wall line, the Parthian marches and the Han frontier are drawn at province resolution. Populations, output (1990 international dollars) and army sizes are rounded estimates with wide uncertainty. Ancient polities are simplified: tribal confederations (Germanic peoples, Sarmatians, Xianbei, Caledonians, Irish kingdoms, Wa, Samhan) are shown as single chiefdom-style states with abs_monarchy government; the Maya city-states are one polity; Saba and Himyar are merged; Kushan and Western Satrap chronology around 117 is uncertain. Peoples outside states (most of the Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, Siberia, the forest zone, Arabia's interior, the Sahara, Tibet, the Tarim basin after the Han withdrawal of 107) are shown as unclaimed land. Flags are invented simple standards.

scenarios.name: Rise of Empires
scenarios.description: November 1444: the day after Varna, where King Władysław of Poland and Hungary fell before Murad II's army, Byzantium is reduced to Constantinople and the Morea, England and France sit out a truce in the Hundred Years' War, Burgundy rules the Low Countries and Ming China, the Timurids and Vijayanagara dominate Asia.
scenarios.approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces, which at this resolution merge many states of 1444: the province of each modern cluster goes to whoever held most of it, so Calais, Ceuta, Ragusa, Siena, Lucca, Mantua, Ferrara, Montferrat, Navarre, Holstein, the Hanseatic cities and most of the Holy Roman Empire's hundreds of lordships, bishoprics and free cities are not shown separately. The Empire's principal states stand for their regions (Bavaria includes Franconia, Württemberg includes Baden and Swabia, the Palatinate includes the electorates of Mainz and Trier, Cologne includes Westphalia, Jülich and Cleves, Saxony includes Thuringia and Magdeburg, Pomerania includes Mecklenburg, Burgundy includes Utrecht and Guelders, which became Burgundian clients only in 1456 and 1473). Some cities fall in a neighbour's province: Constantinople's province includes Kocaeli, so Byzantium looks larger than it was; Genoa's own coast lies in Florence's Tuscan province, so Genoa is shown with Corsica and Chios-Lesbos; Granada is drawn as the Córdoba-Jaén-Granada province, so it appears larger than the Nasrid emirate; Venice's Bergamo and Brescia are Milanese; Franche-Comté is Lorraine's and Bresse Savoy's. Poland and Lithuania, which had separate rulers in November 1444 (Casimir became king of Poland only in 1447), are separate allied countries; Masovia is a Polish subject, Moldavia a Polish subject, Wallachia a Hungarian subject, Cyprus, Dulkadir and the Sharifate of Mecca Mamluk subjects. Serbia and Byzantium paid tribute to the Ottomans but are shown independent so that they do not join the Ottoman war; Candar (Kastamonu) is folded into the Ottoman Empire, Vyatka into Muscovy, Jaffna into Kotte, Navarre into Aragon. The Varna crusade is modelled as a running Hungarian-Ottoman war; the Castilian noble wars, the Old Zürich War, the Soest Feud, the Muscovite civil war and the Saxon Fratricidal War are internal and are shown only as low stability. The Truce of Tours is a non-aggression pact between England and France. Population (millions), GDP (billions of 1990 international dollars, Maddison-style) and army sizes are rounded estimates with wide uncertainty, very wide outside Europe and China. Mamluk Egypt is a military government and the Ashikaga shogunate a military regime; Tibet's regime is shown as a theocracy; steppe khanates, the Gaelic lordships, the Hausa and Mossi kingdoms and the Mixtec-Zapotec states are single decentralised polities. Technology follows the game's Eurasian tree: American societies lag by thousands of years (no iron, horses or wheels), sub-Saharan Africa by centuries. Lands without states of the period are left unowned: most of the Americas and Africa, Siberia, the Wild Fields of Ukraine, Circassia, the Sahara, Arabia's interior, the Turkmen and Baloch tribal lands, Manchuria's Jurchens, Lapland and Greenland (the Norse settlements were gone by c. 1450), Hokkaido, the Philippines and most of the Indonesian islands; Orkney and Shetland, Norwegian until 1468-69, fall in a Scottish province. Flags are simplified standards.

scenarios.name: Concert of Europe
scenarios.description: 20 November 1815: the Second Treaty of Paris closes the Napoleonic Wars and the victors renew their Quadruple Alliance to guard the Vienna settlement. Britain rules the waves, Spain fights rebels from Mexico to the Andes, the Company wars on Nepal and the Ottomans hold the Balkans, while Qing China and Tokugawa Japan look inward.
scenarios.approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces, so each province goes to whoever held most of it on 20 November 1815; many 1815 states are smaller than a province and are folded into a neighbour: Baden and Hohenzollern into Württemberg, Brunswick, Oldenburg and Bremen into Hanover, Hesse-Kassel, Hesse-Darmstadt, Nassau and Frankfurt into one Hesse, the Ernestine duchies, Schwarzburg and Reuss into the Saxon Duchies, the Bavarian Palatinate into Prussia's Rhineland, Holstein, Hamburg and Lübeck into Denmark, Luxembourg into the Netherlands, Kraków into Austria, Parma, Modena and Lucca into Tuscany and the Papal States, Liguria and Savoy follow their provinces (Savoy stays French), the Ionian Islands, Heligoland, Penang, the Gold Coast forts, Gorée and Pondicherry are not shown, and Bukovina goes with Moldavia. Salzburg (handed over by Bavaria in May 1816) is Austrian and French Guiana and Saint-Louis (returned by Portugal and Britain in 1817) are French from the start, and Suriname and the Dutch Antilles (handed back in 1816) Dutch; Java and the Moluccas start British and return to the Dutch by event. Personal unions and vassals are subjects: Hanover of Britain, Congress Poland and Finland of Russia, Norway of Sweden, Egypt, Serbia, Wallachia and Moldavia of the Ottomans, the Lao kingdoms of Siam, Cambodia of Vietnam and Dahomey of Oyo. The Barbary regencies are shown independent, as they were in practice. British India is the East India Company as its own country, allied to Britain, with Hyderabad, Mysore, Travancore and Baroda as its subsidiary-alliance subjects; Awadh is folded into the Company's Uttar Pradesh, Holkar's Indore and Bhopal into Gwalior, the Bhonsle lands of Berar into the Peshwa's Maharashtra, and the Rajput principalities into one Rajput States. The Company is given absolute monarchy as the nearest government type. The Spanish American wars are one war of Spain against the patriot governments still standing (New Granada and the Río de la Plata); royalist-held Mexico, Central America, Venezuela, Quito, Peru, Upper Peru and Chile are Spanish, and the later states are dormant until released by events, which also gives them a truce with Spain. Artigas's Federal League holds the Banda Oriental and the Littoral; Uruguay is not modelled as a later release. The United States is drawn with its states and organised territories east of the Mississippi plus Louisiana, Missouri and Arkansas; the rest of the Louisiana Purchase, the Oregon Country, Rupert's Land, the Great Plains, the Spanish American Amazon, Patagonia, the Chaco and Araucanía, inland Australia, New Zealand, Chukotka, Sakhalin, most of the Kazakh steppe, the Turkmen and Kyrgyz lands, Circassia and Chechnya, the Sahara and the Horn, and most of Africa, the Malay world and the Pacific are unowned: their peoples and many smaller states (the Kazakh hordes, Wadai, the Lunda, Luba and Kongo states, Buganda, the Zulu, Sakalava and Fante polities, the Gulf sheikhdoms, the south Arabian sultanates, Manipur, Ladakh, Perak and Selangor, the Sulu and Bugis sultanates) are not modelled. Brazil's Amazon interior, Spanish Texas, New Mexico and California and Russian Alaska are given to the claimant although control was thin. Tibet and Mongolia are part of the Qing Empire, Ryukyu and Ezo part of Japan, Kashmir and Peshawar part of the Durrani Empire with Kalat folded in. Population (millions) and GDP (billions of 1990 international dollars) are rounded Maddison-style estimates projected back to 1815, including colonies, and are uncertain outside Europe by a third or more; within a country population follows today's distribution, flattened. Armies are rounded post-war peacetime strengths, and both armies and navies are cut by the upkeep caps. Technology lags are judgements. The Quadruple Alliance and the German Confederation (its German members only; the kings of Denmark and the Netherlands belonged for Holstein and Luxembourg alone) are defence blocs; the Holy Alliance is not modelled because it carried no military obligation.

scenarios.name: A House Divided
scenarios.description: 12 April 1861: Confederate guns open on Fort Sumter and the American Civil War begins. Italy has just been proclaimed a kingdom, Prussia and Austria contend for Germany, Napoleon III looks to Mexico, the Taiping hold Nanjing against the Qing and Japan's shogunate totters.
scenarios.approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces, so each province goes to whoever held most of it in April 1861. The Confederacy starts with the seven states of February 1861; Virginia, North Carolina, Tennessee and Arkansas start in the Union and join the Confederacy by an opening event (West Virginia, Kentucky, Missouri, Maryland and Delaware stay Union; Indian Territory is drawn as Union). The US western territories, the Great Plains held in fact by Native nations, Rupert's Land and British Columbia (Hudson's Bay Company and Crown colony, drawn as British), Russian Alaska, Australia's unsettled interior and New Zealand's Maori-held districts are given to the states that claimed them. Natal is not shown: KwaZulu-Natal is one province and goes to the Zulu Kingdom. The German Confederation's minor states are merged: Württemberg with Baden, Saxony with the Thuringian duchies, Hanover with Oldenburg, Brunswick, Mecklenburg and the Hanseatic cities, the Hesses with Nassau and Frankfurt; Rhineland-Palatinate goes to Prussia and Schleswig-Holstein (with Hamburg) to Denmark. Princely India is merged into British India except Hyderabad and Jammu and Kashmir (British subjects); the Ionian Islands (a British protectorate) and Austrian Mantua are too small to draw; Austria holds Venetia as the Udine province and Trentino-South Tyrol as Bozen, and the Papal States are Lazio. The Taiping hold Jiangsu and Anhui. Spain holds Santo Domingo (re-annexed March 1861), Mindanao and Sulu are drawn as Spanish, Siam's Lao and northern Malay vassals and Battambang-Siem Reap are folded into Siam, and Cambodia is a Siamese subject. Lands without states of the period are left unowned: most of interior Africa (including the Yoruba, Benin, Kongo, Lunda, Luba and Lozi polities, which are too fragmented to draw), Patagonia, the Chaco, Araucania, the Turkmen and Pamir lands, Asir, Hadramawt, the Rub al-Khali, New Guinea, Arunachal, the Naga and Mizo hills and the Pacific islands other than Hawaii, Tonga and French Polynesia and New Caledonia. Population (millions) and GDP (billions of 1990 international dollars) are rounded Maddison-style estimates including colonies, and are especially uncertain outside Europe and the Americas; army sizes are rounded start strengths (the Union and the Confederacy only beginning to mobilise). Ongoing internal wars in Colombia and Venezuela, the Nian and Muslim rebellions in China, the Circassian war and the Banjarmasin war are not modelled. Flags are simplified patterns.

scenarios.name: The Great War
scenarios.description: June 1914: the alliance blocs of Europe stand armed and wary, while colonial empires span the globe. One shot in Sarajevo could set the whole system alight.
scenarios.approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces, so each province goes to whoever held most of it in mid-1914 (e.g. Alsace-Lorraine as the Moselle province, Galicia, Bukovina and Transylvania, Western Thrace given to Bulgaria, Dodecanese to Italy, south Sakhalin left with Russia, Kuwait, Qatar and the Trucial States folded into British holdings). Population (millions) and GDP (billions of 1990 international dollars) are rounded Maddison-style estimates that include colonies; army sizes are rounded peacetime strengths; Arabian emirates, Tibet and Mongolia are given their de facto extents. Svalbard and Bouvet Island are left unowned (terra nullius in 1914).

scenarios.name: The Gathering Storm
scenarios.description: January 1936: Germany rearms, Italy fights in Ethiopia, Japan rules Manchuria, and the Soviet Union industrialises at breakneck speed. The peace of Versailles is fraying.
scenarios.approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces, so each province goes to whoever held most of it on 1 January 1936 (e.g. Polish eastern lands as L'viv, Ivano-Frankivs'k, Rivne, Brest, Grodno and Vilnius; Istria and Inner Carniola to Italy; Italian-occupied Tigray to Italy; Jehol and western Manchuria to Manchukuo; south Sakhalin, Danzig, Tangier and Hatay not represented separately). Mandates are owned by the mandatory power. Population (millions) and GDP (billions of 1990 international dollars) are rounded Maddison-style estimates including colonies; army sizes are rounded peacetime strengths (Italy and Ethiopia already mobilised).

scenarios.name: Cold War
scenarios.description: New Year 1962: the Berlin Wall is months old, Cuba has declared for socialism, Algeria and the Congo are in turmoil and the European empires are in their last years, while NATO and the Warsaw Pact face each other across a divided Germany.
scenarios.approximations: Borders follow modern admin-1 provinces: Berlin is drawn wholly as East German, Vietnam is split at province level near the 17th parallel, Kashmir follows the 1949 ceasefire line only roughly, and the Gaza Strip and small enclaves are not shown. Colonies and protectorates still held on 1 January 1962 belong to their metropole (British East Africa, Aden and the Gulf, Portuguese Africa, Algeria, Rwanda-Urundi, West New Guinea, Spanish Sahara); the Central African Federation is a British subject and Katanga is shown as the secessionist state it then was. Population, GDP (Maddison-style 1990 international dollars, including colonies for the empires) and army sizes are rounded estimates; Soviet-bloc and Chinese output is especially uncertain.

scenarios.name: Flashpoint 2035
scenarios.description: A fictional near future, New Year 2035: a crowded multipolar world on edge. Warships shadow each other in the Taiwan Strait, the melting Arctic and a newly independent Greenland draw rival suitors, nuclear-armed India and Pakistan quarrel over Kashmir and the Indus, tankers run a gauntlet at Hormuz, and drought on the Nile meets a war for the Red Sea coast.
scenarios.approximations: Fictional scenario extrapolated from the Modern World (2026). Borders are the 2026 ones except that Greenland has become independent (an invented outcome). Population and GDP are 2026 figures times rough growth multipliers; armies, navies, air forces, nuclear stockpiles and military satellites are plausible extrapolations, not forecasts. The Ethiopia-Eritrea war, the rivalries, the Sahel and AUKUS blocs as defence pacts and all events are invented. Frontier economies start with the first speculative technologies (quantum computing, directed-energy weapons, vertical farming); the rest of the world is a step behind.

scenarios.name: Orbital Age 2085
scenarios.description: A fictional future, New Year 2085: Europe, East Africa, West Africa, South America and Arabia have merged into federations, Korea is one country again and a warmer world has redrawn where people live. Three blocs led by America, China and India hold each other in check with nuclear arsenals and orbital weapons, while their stations, asteroid miners and first settlements on the Moon and Mars make space the new frontier.
scenarios.approximations: Entirely fictional: every merger, alliance, rivalry, technology level and event is invented to make a playable future, not a forecast. Borders are the 2026 provinces regrouped into the invented unions (the European Federation includes the 2026 EU, Ukraine, Moldova and the western Balkans; the federations of East and West Africa, South America and Arabia follow regional organisations; Greenland is independent and Korea reunified). Population and GDP are 2026 figures times rough growth multipliers that stand for demographic change and climate damage (shrinking East Asia and Europe, growing Africa and South Asia, weakened low-lying and very hot states). Forces, nuclear stockpiles and satellites are speculative. Space stations and off-world settlements are given to the space powers by opening events.
